incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — 5xx spike observed on ingress in westus3 (azd2). Affected path: /api/v1/generate. Error rate jumped to ~35% over last 3m. Paging Alex (oncall).

Alex (oncall): Ack. I'm on it. Routing me to net-eng and infra. Maya, any customer-facing reports?

Maya (support): Yes — support tickets coming in: two customers reporting timeouts and 502/503s. Slack #support threads show a surge. Posting a sample error from a customer: 

```
curl -i https://api.redwood.example.com/api/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>"
HTTP/2 502
server: envoy
date: Mon, 15 Mar 2026 14:07:12 GMT
content-type: application/json

{"error":"upstream connect error or disconnect"}
```

Lee (net-eng): Looking at NLB target groups in westus3 azd2. I see a combination of high connection resets and a spike in `connections_active` on the Envoy frontends. Preliminary readout from envoy admin (/stats) below: 

```
cluster.upstream_cx_active: 4200
cluster.upstream_cx_connect_fail: 312
cluster.upstream_cx_connect_timeout: 58
listener.0.0.0.0_443.downstream_cx_destroy: 2100
http.ingress_rq_5xx: 1850
```

Lee (net-eng): NLB targetset NLB-TGT-42 shows many targets UNHEALTHY in azd2 and target connection resets correlate with kernel conntrack exhaustion on those hosts. Also seeing intermittent ALB 502s as Envoy retries fail.

Amy (infra): Thanks Lee. I'm going to check instance conntrack counts and scaling. If conntrack is exhausted we should either increase table size or shift traffic. Quick check on a node: 

```
# on node ip 10.12.3.45
sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
# -> 65536
sudo cat /proc/net/nf_conntrack | wc -l
# -> 65500
```

Amy (infra): We're at the limit. Options: 1) enlarge conntrack table and push sysctl out (fast but might not immediately reduce resets), 2) shift traffic off azd2 to westus2 (safer for customer impact), 3) scale up more ingress nodes in azd2 (may be slow). Joel, what's the tolerance for an emergency region failover?

Joel (prod-lead): Customer impact is moderate — several webhooks failing. I'd prefer option 2 short-term (traffic shift) and option 1 as follow-up. Prep a weighted DNS shift and a routing change in the service router to divert ~60% traffic to westus2 for the next 20m, then re-evaluate. Keep some traffic in azd2 for health checks.

Alex (oncall): Agreed. Lee/Amy — please prepare steps. I'll update status page and notify SRE oncall.

Lee (net-eng): Doing routing change now. For edge routing we have two levers: Route53 weighted record (DNS TTL is 30s) and internal smart-router that can shift by weight instantly. I'll use the smart-router first. Running command: 

```
# increase westus2 weight by 60
curl -X POST https://router-internal.local/api/v1/weights -d '{"route":"/api/v1/generate","weights":{"westus2":0.8,"westus3":0.2}}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ops-token>'
```

Lee (net-eng): Router change applied. Monitoring.

Amy (infra): Pushed conntrack max bump across azd2 nodes and added a temporary cron to flush stale entries. Commands run: 

```
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000
sudo sh -c 'echo 1 > /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_expect_flush'
```

Amy (infra): Also spawned 4 extra ingress-controller-v2 pods (node autoscaler hit a limit, used emergency pool).

Maya (support): Noticing a drop in real-time customer errors in the last 90s. Tickets still flowing but severity reduced. Updating affected customers: we'll note failover in status page.

Alex (oncall): Rolling restart of ingress-controller to pick healthy endpoints in azd2? Joel?

Joel (prod-lead): Yes, do a controlled rolling restart (maxUnavailable 1). Use kubectl rollout restart with the deployment that has the new config.

Amy (infra): Running: 

```
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/ingress-controller-v2
kubectl -n kube-system get pods -w --selector=app=ingress-controller
```

Lee (net-eng): After routing shift and conntrack bump we see 5xx down from ~35% to ~6% over 5m. Envoy connect_fail metrics dropping. Still watching for flappy targets.

Alex (oncall): Good. I'm updating status page: "Partial mitigation in place — traffic shifted to westus2 while we stabilize westus3 azd2. We will continue monitoring and perform postmortem." :memo:

status-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — Reduced error rate detected, customer impact diminished. Next update in 15m or on new development.

Joel (prod-lead): Action items before close: 
- Net-eng to confirm root cause (conntrack exhaustion vs upstream host flapping).
- Infra to audit autoscaling gap that prevented faster node scaling.
- SRE to add alert for conntrack usage > 80% across any AZ.
- Docs: runbook update for instant router weight shift.

Lee (net-eng): I'll capture packet-level traces and correlate with kernel logs, and file a root-cause ticket.

Amy (infra): I'll follow up with a PR to bump default conntrack_max and improve emergency pool scaling.

Maya (support): I'll coordinate with affected customers and close out tickets as their requests resolve.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — 5xx spike mitigated by traffic shift and infra fixes. Time to mitigate: ~22 minutes. Root cause pending investigation.

Alex (oncall): Thanks everyone. Marking as handoff to postmortem owner: Lee. Leaving notes in pager duty and closing the active page. :white_check_mark:

status-bot: Status page updated -> Resolved. Summary posted to #postmortems for writeup.
